scenes.narration: Life isn't too short. We spend too much of it carelessly.
Seneca rejects the common complaint that life is cruelly brief. We're given enough time to do important things, if we arrange it well.
The real problem is leakage: hours drained by distraction, indulgence, and drifting without purpose.
We do not have a very short time, but we lose a great deal of it. Life is long enough for the most important things.
The point stings because it puts the issue back in our hands. A year can feel like nothing when it's spent on autopilot.
Or it can feel rich, when it's aimed at a few things that matter.
Look at yesterday honestly. Estimate how many hours went to things you'd choose again, and how many simply leaked away.
